summary: Both editions were independently reviewed against all seven paragraphs of the selected Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the speaker, conditions, imperatives, negations, mastery claims, and the difficult assertion that the devil has only fear and that his fear has no strength. Contextual “repentance” and the distinct “Turn back” are appropriate. The notes distinguish bracketed editorial supplements from preserved wording, retain the selected working readings, and accurately disclose the alternatives covered by the supplied project reports, including the Vulgata-derived Palatina supplement. Acceptance concerns fidelity to this working source and disclosure of attributed reports; it does not authenticate unseen images, certify external editions, or establish exhaustive collation.
